sentences: Wave64 compute and mesh shaders exact on **any** subgroup size (32-wide NVIDIA, Intel, AMD in wave32 mode), with no subgroup operation at all.
One invocation is still one lane.

Everything a lane needs from the rest of its wave goes through a Workgroup buffer `%x_buf`: votes (`s_cbranch_vccz/vccnz/execz/execnz`, SCC of mask ops, `s_cmp` of masks), whole-mask words (`s_bcnt1`, `s_ff1`, `v_mbcnt`), `v_readlane`, `v_readfirstlane`, `ds_bpermute`, `ds_swizzle`, `v_permlane16/x16`.

The program runs in rounds: in each round every wave that is neither done nor waiting at `s_barrier` runs one segment of its program (a basic block, cut at each cross-lane op), then the whole workgroup meets at one `OpControlBarrier` (Workgroup, AcquireRelease, workgroup + uniform + image memory) that sits in uniform control flow, because every invocation runs every round.

A cross-lane op ends its segment after the lane has stored its value (per-lane data, double-buffered by round parity) or ORed its bit (two mask words per wave, three slots by round mod 3, each slot cleared two rounds after it was read); the code after it runs one round later, when all 64 lanes have written.
SSA values live across a cut go through Function variables.
`s_barrier` is a scheduler state: the wave stops running segments until every wave that isn't done is waiting, which is also how hardware counts finished waves.

A memory access that conflicts with an earlier one in the same segment (read after write, write after read, write after write; LDS and buffer/image memory separately) starts a new round, so two halves of a wave in different subgroups access memory in instruction order, as the lanes of one hardware wave do.

A scalar load (`s_load*`, `s_buffer_load*`) counts as a buffer read: until #1587 it was left out, so a store and a later scalar load of the same address shared a segment and the half in the other subgroup could load before this half had stored (`valu_fuzz.py --family mem --emulate`: lanes 32-63 read the fill pattern after an `s_buffer_load`/`s_load` of the slot lane 0 had written, on RDNA1 RADV and an RTX 5060; `v_readfirstlane_b32`, which gives that slot, already reads the whole wave).

Pinned by `tests/semantic/test_w64x_scalar_load_order.py` (no segment of the emitted rounds accesses buffer memory after a write or writes after a read; three of its five cases fail without the rule).

Confirmed by that CPU test and the ordering argument above; the race does not show on an RX 7900 XTX (AMD 26.10.1 LLPC, Windows 11): `valu_fuzz.py --family mem --seed 5 --programs 21 --wave 64 --emulate` matches 21/21 before and after the rule (3 runs each), so a GPU reproduction on RDNA1/RADV (where #1587 was found) is still pending.
Not ordered: sampling an image the wave wrote.
The missing lanes of a partial last wave read as 0.

Without the flag the output is unchanged, apart from two fixes that apply to every wave64 compute/mesh shader: `v_writelane_b32` selects the lane by the wave lane (on a 32-wide subgroup writes to lanes 32–63 were lost; `cs_w64x_writelane`), and `ds_bpermute_b32` (see the LDS row).

Fewer rounds, same results: a whole-mask read (`s_bcnt1`, `v_mbcnt_lo/hi`, ...) of the value of the same register (or EXEC) that an earlier read in the block already exchanged reuses that exchange (the value's identity is the SSA id last stored to the register, forgotten at block start and at any label); and a block that ends in a voted branch (`s_cbranch_vccz/vccnz/execz/execnz`) runs its successor in the round that reads the vote, since that segment only reads the vote and picks the next block (an inner loop in the scheduler, flag `%x_chain`).

Both rules are pinned by `cs_w64x_mask_reuse` (a mask register and EXEC rewritten between reads), `cs_w64x_mask_reuse2` (EXEC read twice, a read after a buffer store, one half of a mask pair rewritten while the other is kept, a voted branch whose successor starts with a load of the other half's earlier store) and `cs_w64x_chain_barrier` (a voted branch whose successor starts with `s_barrier`, two waves): expected values from the ISA, first run on the AMD 880M with its native 64-wide subgroup, then emulated on both GPUs; `tests/test_translate.py` counts the exchanges in the SPIR-V (one per value, a new one after a rewrite of the register or EXEC), and the translator refuses (`Unsupported`) a voted branch whose segment was not started by the vote's own round.

Under `--wave64-emulate`, `tools/wave64_emulate_opt.py` runs three exact CFG/dataflow passes to eliminate redundant scheduler rounds and global `OpSwitch` blow-up (#884): (1) backward `SCC` liveness skips `scc_from_mask` / `scc_any_half` votes on lane-mask ops (`s_*_saveexec_*`, `s_andn1/andn2_wrexec_*`, `s_and/or/xor/andn2/orn2/nand/nor/xnor/not_b64`, `s_wqm_*`) whenever `SCC` is dead-out (never read before an unconditional overwrite or `s_endpgm`), (2) safe lane-local `s_cbranch_execz`/`execnz` region folding inlines single-entry, single-exit post-dominated regions with no cross-lane ops, no `s_barrier`, no unmasked side effects, no `write_all_lanes` mask spills, no `EXEC`-widening, no live-out scalars, and for each memory domain (`mem`/`lds`) either read-only accesses or an acyclic single write/atomic behind `if (%active)` (issuing any uniform `x_memory_order` split/barrier before the branch — including scalar `s_load*`/`s_buffer_load*` per #1587 — and chaining single-predecessor continuations), and (3) structured emulation (`plan_structured_emulation`, `control_flow = "emulated wave64 structured"`) removes the global round-loop `OpSwitch` on multi-superblock reducible CFGs without non-uniform 32-bit half-mask SCC: single-wave workgroups (`<= 64` threads) run 100% inline structured SPIR-V with direct workgroup barriers (`0` `OpSwitch`, `0` `x_spill`, strictly monotone GEN/KILL 4-bit `dirty_in` memory ordering across blocks and loop back-edges), while multi-wave workgroups (`> 64` threads, without divergent `s_barrier`) emit post-dominating spine blocks and barrier-free guards/loops (including live-out scalars, single-write stores, `EXEC`-widening, and read-only loops) inline and isolate any remaining wave-divergent barrier regions into local mini-schedulers (or a tail scheduler at early `s_endpgm`).

Checked on the CPU by `tests/semantic/test_wave64_emulate_opt.py` (40/64/128/256-thread workgroup interpreter with strict uniform barrier checks, ScreenProbes-shaped chains, nested/reused `saveexec` folds, single-store WAR/RAW ordering, single-wave `inline_all` loop-carried WAR, monotone `dirty_in` regression after `x_round`, multi-wave `structured_hybrid` + local `mini_scheduler`, divergent `s_barrier` fallback, `cs_w64x_saveexec_b64.s` fixture, and negative controls; **not yet GPU-verified** for the structured emulation pass). (1) backward `SCC` liveness skips `scc_from_mask` / `scc_any_half` votes on lane-mask ops (`s_*_saveexec_*`, `s_andn1/andn2_wrexec_*`, `s_and/or/xor/andn2/orn2/nand/nor/xnor/not_b64`, `s_wqm_*`) whenever `SCC` is dead-out (never read before an unconditional overwrite or `s_endpgm`), and (2) safe lane-local `s_cbranch_execz`/`execnz` region folding inlines single-entry, single-exit post-dominated regions with no cross-lane ops, no `s_barrier`, no memory/LDS writes, no unmasked side effects, no `write_all_lanes` mask spills, no `EXEC`-widening, and no live-out scalars behind `if (%active)` (issuing any uniform `x_memory_order` split before the branch — including scalar `s_load*`/`s_buffer_load*` per #1587 — and chaining single-predecessor continuations), keeping all 64 lanes of each wave in the same scheduler round.

Checked on the CPU by `tests/semantic/test_wave64_emulate_opt.py` (64-thread and 128-thread workgroup interpreter with uniform barrier checks, ScreenProbes-shaped chains, nested/reused `saveexec` folds, internal loop, `cs_w64x_saveexec_b64.s` fixture, RAW memory/scalar-load ordering, and negative controls for live-out scalars, stores, cross-lane ops, and EXEC-widening).
`scripts/bench_wave64.py` times `cs_bench_mix` native and emulated and checks the emulated output bytes against the native AMD run.
Cost: one workgroup barrier per segment, and `%x_buf` = (2·L + 6·W + 7) dwords for L invocations in W waves, counted in `lds_bytes`.

GPU-checked on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop (subgroup 32, driver 617.42) and AMD Radeon 880M (subgroup 64, AMD driver 26.11.2 LLPC): `check.py` 38/39 (the mesh test runs in the other script) and `scripts/run_gpu_tests.py` 40/40 on both with `LEONIDA_W64_EMULATE=1`, including every wave64 test (`cs_wavemask`, `cs_wave64_ballot`, `cs_wm_*`) and the cross-half suite `cs_w64x_*` / `ms_w64x_ballot`: readlane and writelane at lanes ≥ 32, readfirstlane with only upper lanes active, branches voted by one lane of either half, ballot + `v_mbcnt_lo/hi` compaction over 64 lanes (also in a mesh shader, 4096/4096 pixels), a 128-thread workgroup whose two waves take different branches, `s_barrier` between waves with different loop counts, LDS read-after-write and write-after-read across the halves without a barrier, a load, ballot and load in one block, and a partial wave (group 40).
Without the flag the same RTX 5070 passes 19/37 (the wave64 tests skip there).
Not covered: VS/PS/GS (no workgroup memory or barrier there).

Known driver bug: AMD's Windows shader compiler for RDNA2 crashes (access violation in `vkCreateComputePipelines`) on many emulated compute shaders with LDS (#857: drivers 32.0.21030 to 32.0.21045.29003, iGPUs and RX 6000; 23.20.44, RDNA3, RDNA4, RADV and NVIDIA are fine), so `make_game.py --wave64-emulate auto` leaves emulation off when the runtime's GPU is such a device and runs wave64 natively (`rdna2_amd_windows` in `tools/vk_subgroup_info.py`, by PCI device ID and driver ID).
